# Market Research

`sales.market_and_targeting.market_research` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

**What market exists here, who already serves it, and on what terms does it buy?**


> Establishing the shape of a market before committing a motion to it: which buying populations exist inside it, who already holds the budget they would spend with us, what those buyers currently pay and on what terms, how they buy, and how much of the category they already understand. The unit of analysis is a buying behaviour shared by many companies — never a single account, and never a database query result. It is NOT ICP definition, which narrows an already-chosen market to the accounts that win AND retain with us, and which needs our own outcome history to say anything at all. It is NOT TAM/SAM/SOM, which sizes a market that this capability has already shaped — a size computed before a map is arithmetic performed on a guess. It is NOT account research, which studies one named company the week before someone contacts it. And it is not competitive intelligence: knowing what a rival ships is a fraction of knowing why a segment moved budget to them.

> Six objects, not forty, and deliberately no deal-execution knowledge. Decision Maker, Champion, Buying Committee, Budget and Timeline are all authored and all excluded: they describe one live purchase, and the subject here is a population that mostly has no deals in it yet. Loading them would let a market-research compile drift into running the deal that produced the evidence, which is the opposite of what this capability is for — the deal is the sample, not the subject. Note also what is absent from core: there is no `market_segment` object. Segments live as a property of market_map because the core/scoped rule is decided by the reference graph, and nothing outside this capability loads a segment today. If tam_sam_som or territory_planning ever needs one, it should be promoted straight to objects/core/ rather than copied.

## Outcomes

- Segments named and separated by how they buy — budget owner, committee shape, cycle, procurement posture. Two populations that buy the same way are one segment however different their industry codes look.
- The incumbent set mapped, with the do-nothing option named as an incumbent rather than left off the board. Where the budget goes today is the only competitor question that changes a plan.
- Prevailing commercial terms established: what the segment already pays for this job, what it is charged BY, and what contract shape it expects. Our own commercial design is constrained by these, not by our cost base.
- Category maturity established — whether buyers are unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware or comparing vendors — because that, not deal size, decides which motion is affordable.
- An explicit entry verdict per segment: enter, pilot, defer, or decline. The negative verdict is the outcome that pays for the capability; a research function that has never recommended against a market is describing markets, not choosing between them.
- Every load-bearing claim dated, sourced, and carrying the specific observation that would overturn it, so the map can be checked later instead of believed later.


## Failure modes

- Confusing a market with a list. A filter query returns companies; a market is a shared job bought in a shared way, and the query captures neither. The list looks like progress because it is countable.
- Sizing before segmenting. An industry total multiplied by an assumed penetration rate, then quoted in a board deck as evidence. The arithmetic is sound and every input is a belief.
- Sampling our own funnel. Interviewing the people who already replied to us and calling the result a market view. It is a view of the motion we already run, which is precisely the thing the research was supposed to test. The accounts that chose the incumbent and the ones that did nothing hold the information.
- Reading an empty category as an open one. No competitors far more often means a population that does not buy this at all than a population nobody has found; the cost of teaching a market that a category exists lands entirely on whoever goes first.
- Interviewing for opinion instead of behaviour. 'Would you buy this?' reliably produces a courteous yes. 'What did you do the last time this happened, who signed it, and what did it cost you?' produces facts, because it asks about a transaction that already occurred.
- Research with no expiry. Incumbent pricing, packaging and buyer priorities move within quarters; a map assembled once is still being cited as fact long after every load-bearing claim in it stopped being true, and nothing in the artefact says so.

## KPIs

| KPI | Unit | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| segment_win_rate_spread | percent | higher_is_better | Gap between the best and worst researched segment. A flat spread means the segmentation is not segmenting and the map has no operational content. |
| segments_declined | count | higher_is_better | Segments explicitly recommended against. Near zero means the capability describes markets instead of choosing between them. |
| cycle_length_forecast_error | percent | lower_is_better | Researched cycle length against observed. The single best test of whether a segment's buying process was actually understood rather than assumed. |
| finding_falsification_rate | percent | target_band | Share of load-bearing findings later contradicted in the field. Zero means nobody is checking, not that the research was right; very high means the sampling is broken. |
| map_staleness | days | lower_is_better | Age of the oldest load-bearing claim still being cited in a live decision. |
| research_to_first_pipeline | days | lower_is_better | Elapsed time from entry verdict to first qualified pipeline in that segment. Measures whether the map was actionable or merely interesting. |

owner **Sales** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Two scoped objects carry this capability's inference: market_map and market_finding, with twenty-three patterns between them of which eleven are executable and twelve are blocked. The single highest-value signal gap is cross-account aggregation — a segment key on the account plus a derived aggregate over it. Every predicate in the grammar is evaluated against one node and its one-hop neighbours, so a capability whose subject is a population is currently forced to infer that population from one deal at a time. That one addition would unblock most of the blocked half here and in tam_sam_som and icp_definition too. Note also that only field-feedback situations bind: nothing Layer 2 emits fires before a deal exists, which is where most of this capability actually lives.
